findings.summary: The right-triangle formulas used abbreviated side labels and one inconsistent gender form instead of the established French terminology.
evidence: The explanatory paragraph used côté opposé and côté adjacent, while the formulas displayed opposé and adjacent.
findings.resolution: Aligned all three formulas with côté opposé, côté adjacent, and hypoténuse.

findings.summary: The inverse-trigonometry formulas retained English side labels in the French presentation.
evidence: The formulas displayed opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse in an otherwise French section.
findings.resolution: Localized all three inverse formulas with the established French side terminology.

findings.summary: The worked trigonometry example used shortened side labels instead of the terms used in the surrounding French explanation.
evidence: The example labels were opposé and adjacent while the section consistently described the sides as côté opposé and côté adjacent.
findings.resolution: Expanded both example labels to côté opposé and côté adjacent.
